units.en: In addition to regular, motorized, and mechanized infantry, there are three specialized infantry types, known as ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ (not to be confused with the ⟦2⟧ Superior Firepower): ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, and ⟦5⟧. These units are useful in specific situations. They only require standard infantry equipment, but tend to require more of it compared to ⟦6⟧.

⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ units also count as special forces units. The former are closer to ⟦2⟧ units than to ⟦3⟧ and require their own, specialized ⟦4⟧. The latter are armored units that rely on ⟦5⟧. With ⟦6⟧, they can also be built out of ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧, and ⟦9⟧ chasses using the ⟦10⟧.

Each country has a special forces cap that dictates the maximum amount of special forces battalions they are allowed to field. This cap is the greater of either 24⟦0⟧ battalions or 5%⟦1⟧ of the total amount of non-SF battalions making up the rest of your deployed divisions. Divisions cannot be changed, trained, given a different template or have their template adjusted if that would result in exceeding the SF cap. By default, to increase the SF cap beyond the default 24 without any bonuses, you would have to exceed the 480 non-SF battalion breakeven point by 20 for each additional SF battalion. For example, you would need 500 non-SF battalions for 25 SF battalions, 520 non-SF battalions for 26 SF battalions, 540 non-SF battalions for 27 SF battalions, etc. These battalions do not need to be fully equipped or be at full strength, they just need to be part of divisions that are deployed in the field.

Special forces cap can also be increased through certain ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, and ⟦3⟧ that affect national spirits. With ⟦4⟧, the amount of special forces that can be fielded can be increased through special forces doctrines, both by increasing special forces cap and by decreasing the contribution of certain units to that cap. Without ⟦5⟧, special forces cap can be increased with the ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧ technology.

⟦0⟧ are specialized infantry trained to engage in wet terrain and perform amphibious invasions. They receive bonuses when attacking over wet ⟦1⟧ and during ⟦2⟧. Marine units are very effective when supported by ⟦3⟧ or their ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧, or ⟦6⟧ cousins.

Marines ITroops specializing in amphibious warfare are growing ever more indispensable. Improvised methods and equipment become things of the past as our naval infantry is supported by specialized landing craft and training.
Marines IIAmphibious warfare requires constant innovation. Improved logistical support and portable harbors can enable our marines to perform landings that may otherwise have been impossible.
Marines IIIMarines can be more than just amphibious infantry. In the future, our marine corps will be among the most disciplined and organized special forces.
⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ are specialized infantry that excel in maneuvering through and engaging in rough ⟦2⟧, such as ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧.

Mountain Infantry ICombat in mountain ranges exposes troops to many perils, but sometimes cannot be avoided. We can minimize these risks by providing our soldiers with specialized training for this environment.

Mountain Infantry IIGoing beyond survival, our forces can be trained to use mountains to their advantage. With light equipment and mule transports, they can maneuver in this terrain better than other infantry.
Mountain Infantry IIIPreparing for the most arduous mountain missions in high altitudes and low temperatures will require extraordinary training and discipline from our mountain troops.

⟦0⟧ are the only type of unit that can be ⟦1⟧ into the field, which they do via transport plane. This allows them to perform operations behind enemy lines and in locations where other units cannot easily reach. It is important to note that divisions that mix ⟦2⟧ with other line battalions cannot be ⟦3⟧.
The AI will use paratroopers in battle, but never uses them for paradrops.
Paratroopers IBy incorporating airborne forces into our army, we can make forced entries and position key troops in previously inaccessible areas, allowing for new tactical opportunities.

Paratroopers IITransitioning from small operations with only a few paratroopers to larger airborne divisions paves way for massive airborne landings, taking these forces beyond a novelty to a natural part of warfare.

Paratroopers IIILearning to adapt paradrop operations according to weather, standardizing equipment such as jump boots and extended specialized training will minimize the confusion and risks involved in these dangerous missions.
For ⟦0⟧ doctrines, see Special forces doctrine

These technologies increase the capabilities, and potentially also the number, of special forces units. The first tech will give them a boost to acclimatization speed. Afterwards, the tree splits into two options. One option is to train your special forces harder, to improve their skills and their ability to fight for longer before having to be resupplied. The other option is to expand the special forces training programs to accept more recruits: your special forces will be more numerous, but come with more drag and not quite as high speed. In the end, though, they will still be elite forces and will be able to develop training to make them even more skilled in fighting in the harshest of conditions.
Special ForcesUnconventional fighting requires specialist training. We need to ensure that our troops are prepared and able to adapt to harsh conditions.
